To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following methods are effective in recruiting patients for screening for lung cancer: (1) a letter from a physician to the patient's home, (2) telephone calls to the patient by the screener, (3) a letter from the screener to the patient's family members, and (4) a letter to patients from the physician's office.

the most effective recruitment methods are: (a) face-to-face contact with the potential participant; (b) use of an invitation letter from the physician; (c) the use of a brochure that includes a personal letter from the physician and a description of the study; (d) the use of an educational pamphlet; (e) the use of the telephone to contact potential participants; and (f) the use of newspaper advertising.

the following recruitment methods were effective in recruiting participants for lung cancer screening: 1) a letter sent to all members of the primary care clinic, 2) a letter sent by a primary care physician, 3) a letter sent from a nurse, and 4) a letter sent in the mail.
